source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.10
text: Processed rice starch, refined into fine granular or powder form, can be sold into the pharmaceutical industry as a 'tablet filler' — an inert bulking/binding ingredient (excipient) used in manufacturing compressed medicine tablets. The slide illustrates this with scanning-electron-microscope images of rice starch granules and a compressed powder sample alongside a photo of assorted colored pharmaceutical tablets. This shows that rice starch has a non-food industrial market in pharmaceutical manufacturing, offering a potentially higher-value outlet for surplus rice or rice starch beyond food use, though entering this market would require food/pharma-grade processing and quality standards not detailed in the slide.
